title: Direct TBC Use as a Collision-Resistant TCC
summary: A tweakable blockcipher admits an inverse-based collision in the TCC role; determining whether direct TBC use can satisfy collision resistance remains the stated task.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether a tweakable blockcipher (TBC), which has the syntax of the target TCC primitive, can be used directly in the TCC role while satisfying collision resistance. The central limitation is a collision attack on a TBC $F$: choose arbitrary $CK$ and $D_1$, choose distinct tweaks $T_1$ and $T_2$, and set $D_2 \leftarrow F.\operatorname{Inv}(CK,T_2,F.\operatorname{Ev}(CK,T_1,D_1))$; then $(CK,T_1,D_1)$ and $(CK,T_2,D_2)$ form a collision, so $F$ is not collision resistant.

scope.domain: Collision resistance of tweakable blockciphers used directly as TCC primitives.
parameters: F: the tweakable blockcipher considered in the TCC role
D₁ and D₂: data values related by evaluation and inverse evaluation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a tweakable blockcipher can be used directly in the TCC role while satisfying collision resistance.

citations.label: A Universal Transform for Committing Authenticated Encryption

progress.summary: The source asks why a syntactically compatible TBC cannot serve directly as the TCC. It then gives an inverse-based collision showing that the TBC is not collision resistant.
